rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act statewide rent increase cap
rules.requirement: Owners may not raise gross rent over any 12-month period by more than 5% plus the regional CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower, measured from the lowest rent charged in the prior 12 months. Increases are limited to two per 12-month period, and rent may be reset freely on a new tenancy where no prior tenant remains.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property (including mobilehome park units) statewide, unless covered by a stricter local rent control law or another exemption. Mobilehome tenancies are covered for increases on or after February 18, 2021.
rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; school or university dormitories; housing under stricter local rent control; housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); separately alienable units such as single-family homes and condos not owned by a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, provided the statutory exemption notice was given; owner-occupied duplexes where neither unit is an ADU/JADU; mobilehome homeowners as defined in Section 798.9.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Single-family/condo exemption requires a non-corporate owner and written exemption notice to tenants. Owner-occupied duplex exemption requires owner occupancy at the start of the tenancy. Deed-restricted affordable or subsidized housing is excluded. The initial rent on a new tenancy with no remaining prior tenant is not capped.

rules.penalty: Civil action by the tenant for injunctive relief, damages equal to the overcharge, discretionary attorney's fees and costs, and up to three times the overcharge for willful, oppressive, fraudulent, or malicious conduct. The Attorney General, city attorney, or county counsel may enforce. Three-year statute of limitations, and waivers are void.
rules.quoted_span: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.
rules.conflict_note: The current text was added by SB 567 (Stats. 2023, Ch. 290), effective January 1, 2024 and operative April 1, 2024. The cap itself applies to rent increases on or after March 15, 2019 (mobilehomes: February 18, 2021), originally under AB 1482. The section sunsets and is repealed as of January 1, 2030.
